main_text.p: Et omne sicinum solum, misero, precor, Concede patri ne sit ipse carnifex, Hunc cadat alter quem soles, lubens feram.
main_text.head: SATHANAS.
main_text.p: Non dicta mutabunt Superi, tua cadet Ifacus ecce dextera, sel impie Rebellis illorum excides fauoribus.
main_text.head: ABRAHAMVS.
main_text.p: O, quum reuerti me mea solum siderit, Quid dicet sxor? quum perisse filium Sciet genitoris interemptum dextera? Quum luctuosas horridis slulatibus Replebit ædes mater, atque sæpius Suas Isacum delitiàs frustra socans Fletus acerbos fundet? O, tantos quibus Verbis dolores leniam? Si te, Deus, Hanc imperasse dixerim cadem, meis Habere quis solet fidem sermonibus? Si nemo tuis factam auspiciis illam putet, Mox mox per srbes cursibus solans citis Me parricidam fama dicet impium, Diras ꝯ omnis impre cata gens truces Manus, nefasque patris execrabitur. Quis pollicenti tibi bona plura credet, Quis nomen inuocare post tuum solet, Promissa si præstare temnis? ꝯ suos Cruore natorum imperas cultros patrem Fœdare: si iura gentium præcordiis Infculpta conuellens hominem sanguisimi

page.notes: Printed text is in a 16th–17th century Latin verse drama; some letters (s for long s and s/f forms) are uncertain; the words "Diras ꝯ omnis impre cata" and "Quis pollicenti" are read with doubt; marks ꝯ are printed ampersand-like signs. The bottom line reads partly as a catchword-like mark "V" and a small mark "ꝯ"; the final word "sanguisimi" is cut at the page edge and may be read as [?].
